subject: Buenavista evaluation: success criteria & POC runbook
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marta Reyes <marta@buenavista.com>, Luis Ortega <eng-lead@buenavista.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-02T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Buenavista evaluation: success criteria & POC runbook

Hi Marta / Luis — great to connect today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed plan so we have a single source of truth to move the trial forward. Please flag anything I missed.

Call recap (agreed):
- Goal: Validate Redwood Inference can replace the current on-prem reranking pipeline for invoice extraction and improve latency/cost by >= 30% while preserving extraction accuracy.
- Scope: 3-week evaluation using a redacted slice of Buenavista invoice traffic (no PII) + synthetic edge cases.

Success criteria (agreed on call):
1) Extraction accuracy (F1) >= current baseline - 2 points on supplier names + line items
2) 95th percentile latency <= 450ms on a 1k qps simulated burst for the reranker stage
3) Average per-invoice token cost reduced by >= 30% vs baseline
4) No PII retained beyond session; confirm delete-on-idle and KV cache policies

Proposed evaluation plan & timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): provisioning & access — Redwood provisions a sandbox tenant and uploads initial ingestion connector. Owner: Ben Carter (SE).
- Week 1 (Aug 9–15): Ingest sample, run baseline inference, collect metrics. Owner: Buenavista eng + Ben.
- Week 2 (Aug 16–22): Scenario tests (edge cases, flood-burst latency tests). Owner: Buenavista eng + Marissa (CS).
- Week 3 (Aug 23–29): Acceptance run (comparing outputs, final performance report), decision and next steps. Owner: Marta (product) + Soojin (AE).

Immediate next steps (action owners):
- Ben: provide provisioning checklist and environment build window (attached).
- Marta: share procurement contact if procurement needs to start paperwork pre-POC.
- Buenavista: identify 10–15 sample invoices and a redaction contact for the dataset.
- Soojin: circulate evaluation metrics workbook and schedule weekly check-ins (we propose Thursdays 10am PT).

Attachments: Redwood POC provisioning checklist (redwood-poc-provisioning-checklist.pdf), evaluation metrics template (buenavista-eval-metrics.xlsx).

Thanks — I’ll put the calendar hold for Thu 8/5 10am PT for initial sync; if that doesn’t work please suggest alternatives.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Marta Reyes <marta@buenavista.com>

Date: 2027-08-03T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Buenavista evaluation: success criteria & POC runbook

Thanks, Soojin — this is helpful and aligned. A couple quick asks from procurement and security: 

- Can you share a SOC 2 report or security pack we can drop into our vendor intake? (we need the link or a zip)
- Data residency: the sample must remain within our US region and any persisted artifacts must be deletable on demand.
- Procurement: please loop in our procurement lead (procure@buenavista.com) — they’ll want an SOW template and an expected cost range for the 3-week trial.

Also, the 95th percentile latency target is critical for our internal SLA. Can you confirm whether the 450ms target is achievable on your hosted tiers or if we should plan for a dedicated pool?

Appreciate it — I’ll gather the sample invoices and redaction guidance this week.

— Marta
Product Manager | Buenavista Logistics
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marta Reyes <marta@buenavista.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-04T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Buenavista evaluation: success criteria & POC runbook

Marta — quick answers and what I’ll deliver by EOD Friday: 

1) SOC2 / security pack: attaching our security pack (redwood-security-pack.zip) which includes SOC 2 Type II summary, data handling, and encryption details.
2) Data residency/encryption: we can provision a US-region sandbox (us-west-2) and enforce encryption at rest + tenant-level key controls. Deletion on idle/session is supported; I’ll include config steps in the checklist.
3) Latency: for 95th <= 450ms on 1k qps burst, we recommend a small dedicated pool for the acceptance run — hosted tiers may be fine for baseline but not peak bursts we plan to simulate. I’ll include cost delta options in the runbook.

Planned deliverables (Ben):
- Provisioning checklist + infra commands (attached: redwood-poc-provisioning-checklist.pdf)
- Small script to run synthetic burst tests and collect p95/p99 (will push to shared Drive)
- Quick FR for dedicated pool sizing recommendation and cost estimate

Proposed build window: Tue Aug 10 9am–12pm PT (allows us to validate connectivity before Week 1). Please confirm.

Thanks — I’ll post the Drive links once the script is in.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Luis Ortega <eng-lead@buenavista.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marta Reyes <marta@buenavista.com>
Date: 2027-08-10T11:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Buenavista evaluation: success criteria & POC runbook

Thanks — tightening up a couple operational asks from our side: 

- Can the acceptance run be moved up a week? We have a vendor review on Aug 24 and it would be great to have preliminary results before that if possible.
- For the latency test, please confirm the test harness will simulate our real traffic distribution (we can share a brief replay script). We need p95 and p99 under the same ingress shapes.
- Encryption at rest is a must; we’ll want confirmation that keys are customer-managed or an explanation of controls if not.

If you can confirm the earlier acceptance window (and the build window still works), we’ll prioritize the sample extraction.

Hi Marta / Luis — friendly status nudge and short plan to keep momentum. I know schedules got tight in Aug; below is where we stand and the asks to unblock Week 2 acceleration.

Completed since last thread: 
- Ben provisioned the US sandbox and shared the provisioning checklist + burst-test script (links above).
- Security pack uploaded (SOC 2 excerpt + controls) — Ben attached the ZIP earlier.
- Buenavista redaction rules and 12 sample invoices received (thanks, Marta).

Open items / blockers (owners + ask):
1) Procurement contact & PO SOW signoff (Owner: Marta / Buenavista procurement). Status: procurement email not yet looped. Ask: please confirm contact by EOD Wed 9/1 so procurement can begin.
2) Decision on dedicated pool for acceptance run (Owner: Soojin + Ben). Ask: Ben to confirm sizing / cost delta; Marta/Luis to confirm whether budget allows (we can still run scaled-down burst on hosted but p95 will differ).
3) Replay harness for ingress shape (Owner: Luis). Ask: share the replay script or a 30-min sample by 9/2 so Ben can validate test fidelity.

Proposed near-term schedule if blockers cleared: 
- Sep 1–3: Week 1 continued — ingestion validation & baseline runs
- Sep 6–10: Week 2 — burst & edge-case tests (acceptance window)
- Sep 13: Deliverable: acceptance report and recommended production configuration

If the Aug 24 vendor review is still a hard deadline, we can do a focused acceptance snapshot the week of Sep 6 and share preliminary numbers earlier — please confirm which date you prefer.

Thanks — short ask: can I get procurement contact and replay sample by 9/2? I’ll keep a standing 15-minute sync Thu 10am PT if that helps keep rapid feedback loops.
